recipes.name: Fiesta Salsa
ingredients_raw: 0.25 cup Ball® Fiesta Salsa Mix - MIX WELL BEFORE MEASURING

steps.text: Inspect 2 pint-sized jars for cracks and rings for rust, discarding any defective ones. Immerse in simmering water until salsa is ready. Wash new, unused lids and rings in warm, soapy water.
Combine tomatoes, fiesta salsa mix, and vinegar in a large saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat, and simmer for 5 minutes.

Pack hot salsa into hot, sterilized jars, filling to within ½ inch of tops. Run a clean knife or thin spatula around insides of jars to remove any air bubbles. Wipe rims with a moist paper towel to remove any residue. Top with lids and screw on rings tightly.

Place a rack in the bottom of a large stockpot and fill halfway with water. Bring to a boil and lower jars 2 inches apart into the boiling water using a holder. Pour in more boiling water to cover jars by at least 1 inch. Bring to a rolling boil, cover, and process for 35 minutes.

Remove jars from the pot and let rest, several inches apart, for 12 to 24 hours. Press centers of each lid with a finger to ensure lids do not move up or down. Remove rings for storage and store in a cool, dark area.

raw_recipe.headline: Fiesta Salsa
raw_recipe.description: For this recipe, use a store-bought fiesta salsa mix to turn your ripe, juicy tomatoes (or canned ones if fresh aren't available) into a tasty salsa.

review.reviewBody: This is good but watery. Make sure you drain your tomatoes through a cheese cloth first. Not too spicy and it has a good flavor.
Great recipe, I did add to it, (lime juice, chipotle powder, pineapple, papaya, (to give it a sweet n spicy flavor)purple onion) 👍
We’ve made this several times and loved it!! We added onions, sweet and hot peppers. It’s soooo good!
